Call recap (high level)
- Goal: run Redwood Private in an air-gapped datacenter for ML inference (customer data never leaves site)
- Primary workload: low-latency chat and batch embedding jobs for fraud detection and compliance (peak concurrent requests ~200 QPS, shorter sequence lengths)
- Preference: start with a 4-node GPU cluster, expand to dedicated capacity depending on load

Open items / requests from our side
1) Hardware details: exact GPU model(s), count per rack, CPU/RAM, NVMe / shared storage plan
2) Upgrade & patching constraints: do you require zero-outbound upgrades (i.e., full offline upgrades via physically delivered artifacts)? Any blackout windows?
3) Ops model: will your infra team manage day-to-day (images, backups, node reboots) or do you want Redwood to provide on-site/remote assist during initial rollout?
4) Telemetry & telemetry blocking: can you share the policy on telemetry/phone-home for licensing and health checks (we support opt-out and local-only logs for air-gapped installs)

Next steps

- Redwood: we’ll produce an SOW + suggested cluster topology and offline upgrade playbook once hardware is confirmed.

Paul — great, thanks for the details — that baseline is very workable. A few confirmations and recommendations from our side: 

1) GPU / cluster topology
- A100 80GB is fully supported. For your peak of ~200 QPS with short sequences, a 4-node single-GPU-per-host cluster should be a reasonable starting point; we’ll include performance tuning and batching recommendations in the SOW.

2) Storage & model placement
- Recommend keeping model artifacts and larger checkpoints on your NAS (50TB) and using local NVMe for hot model copies & KV cache. We’ll provide scripts to synchronize model bundles during planned maintenance windows.

3) Offline upgrades & packaging
- We support fully offline upgrades: we produce signed upgrade bundles (container images + control-plane artifacts + checksums) that your infra team imports. No phone-home required.
- Typical upgrade flow we propose:
  a) Redwood prepares signed bundle and verification manifest.
  b) Customer transfers bundle to internal artifact repo (or USB) and verifies signatures.
  c) During maintenance window, infra runs a staged rollout; each node has a rollback snapshot.

4) Telemetry & KMS
- We support integration with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) and can operate without outbound telemetry. For health/usage monitoring we can ship a local collector that writes to your ELK.

5) Support & professional services
- We offer an assisted install option (onsite or remote) for the initial rollout. We’ll include a week of on-call support and an optional onsite engineer in the SOW.

I’ve attached the updated spec and a mutual action (MA) template to start SOW scoping. If you can confirm (a) preferred maintenance window, (b) whether you want assisted install, and (c) who will own KMS/HSM integration, we’ll draft the SOW and forward to procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa
